title: Pick the right mount
prompt: You're reviewing storage choices in the notes-api Compose stack. Select **every** pairing of need and mount type that is correct.
hints: Ask two questions of each: should the data survive the container, and does it come from your repository?
A named volume never reflects edits you make in your editor; a tmpfs never survives a stop.
explanation: Postgres data belongs in a named volume: it survives `down` and avoids host permission and performance issues. Seed scripts live in the repo, so a read-only bind mount into `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d` is right. Disposable scratch space is what tmpfs is for. A named volume for `src/` would freeze a copy of your code that never sees your edits, and tmpfs for data you want to keep loses it on every stop.

pg-named.text: Postgres data that must survive restarts → named volume `pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`
pg-named.why: Correct. Named volumes outlive containers and are Docker-managed.

init-bind.text: SQL schema scripts from the repository → bind mount `./db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro`
init-bind.why: Correct. The files live in your repo and the container only needs to read them.

src-volume.why: A named volume is filled once and then independent of your host folder, so edits never reach the container. Use Compose watch or a bind mount.

pg-tmpfs.text: Postgres data you want to keep between workdays → `tmpfs: /var/lib/postgresql/data`
pg-tmpfs.why: tmpfs lives in memory; stopping the container erases it.

tmpfs-scratch.text: Temporary files for a test run that should vanish afterwards → `tmpfs: /tmp/scratch`
tmpfs-scratch.why: Correct. Fast, never written to disk, gone when the container stops.
